messages.text:
We propose replacing the adviser, copying and audit provisions with the following wording.

**Purpose and access.** The testing house may use the drawings and CAD files solely to prepare for, conduct and report on the agreed actuator vibration tests. Before access, the parties must approve a written list naming each person who needs the material and their role in the tests. This applies to employees, contractors and external advisers. Each listed person must be bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement. The testing house is responsible for their compliance. Additions and substitutions require the design owner’s written approval before access.

**Copies and fixtures.** The testing house may make the minimum working copies needed for the tests. It must encrypt digital copies at rest and in transit and restrict access to the approved personnel. It may extract only the geometry needed to design and fabricate fixtures for the agreed tests. The same access and use restrictions apply to fixture files and physical fixtures. The testing house may not reuse the drawings, geometry, fixture files or fixtures for another project or use them to develop or assist in developing a competing product.

**Closeout and verification.** Within 30 days after the design owner accepts the final test report in writing, or after earlier termination of the tests, the testing house must delete the drawings, CAD files, working copies and fixture files in its possession or control, including copies held by approved external personnel, and physically destroy the derivative fixtures. It may retain the accepted report if it contains no recoverable CAD geometry. Within the same period, an independent verifier agreed by both parties must certify in writing what was destroyed, by what method and on what date, identifying any exceptions. That certificate will satisfy the design owner’s verification requirement without site access.

Can your facility work with that closeout trigger and certification deadline? If a backup cycle or test-record requirement prevents full destruction within 30 days, please identify the specific material and minimum retention period so we can agree a narrow exception.

We can meet a 30-day closeout deadline for working files and fixtures, including those held by our specialists. We propose a fallback if report acceptance remains outstanding, and a certificate from our test manager as the first step in verification. We need a two-year exception for calibration records. We are not requesting a backup exception.

**Access attachment.** “Before disclosure, the parties will approve an attachment naming the testing house personnel, specialist machining shop, accredited laboratory and individual recipients. For each recipient, the attachment will state the task and the files or extracts they may receive. The shop may receive only the fixture fabrication extract. The lab may receive only the extracts needed for setup and testing. The testing house will isolate those extracts from the source files and apply the agreed confidentiality, encryption and use restrictions.”

**Substitutions.** “The testing house may submit a replacement specialist or individual by email, identifying the replacement, qualifications, task and proposed access. The design owner will approve or give reasons for refusal within three business days and will not unreasonably withhold approval where qualifications and safeguards are equivalent. Email approval updates the attachment. The replacement may receive material only after approval. The testing house will revoke outgoing access when the handover ends and obtain written confirmation that the outgoing specialist has returned or destroyed its copies.”

**Closeout attachment.** “The 30-day period starts on written acceptance of the final report, earlier termination, or expiry of ten business days after delivery of the final report without a written request identifying a correction that requires continued access to the drawings, whichever occurs first. A timely request permits retention only of material needed for that correction. The same review period applies to the corrected report. The testing house may retain the agreed geometry-free report and calibration records for two years from the relevant calibration date. Calibration records may identify the equipment, calibration date, results and certificate reference. They must contain no drawings, fixture dimensions or recoverable geometry.” The two-year limit applies to the calibration records only.

**Verification.** “Within the 30-day period, the test manager will certify the disposition of the files, extracts and fixtures listed in the attachments, identifying the method, date and any outstanding item. The certificate will incorporate written confirmations from the shop and lab and identify retained calibration records and their expiry dates. If the design owner identifies a specific discrepancy that the testing house cannot resolve with documentary evidence, a mutually agreed independent verifier may review the relevant records remotely and report its findings to both parties. Verification confers no right of entry to a shared customer site.”

Would the certificate backed by both specialists’ confirmations meet your routine verification requirement, with independent review available for an unresolved discrepancy?

Yes. We accept the test manager’s certificate, backed by written confirmations from the shop and lab, as routine proof of destruction. We accept remote independent review for an unresolved discrepancy and agree that verification confers no right of site entry. We propose the following wording to make that review available when needed.

> If the design owner identifies a specific gap or discrepancy in the certificate or supporting confirmations, the testing house will provide documentary evidence addressing it within ten business days. If the issue remains unresolved, either party may require a remote review by a mutually agreed independent verifier. The testing house will make the relevant disposition records available to the verifier, including those from its specialists. The verifier will report to both parties. Listing an outstanding item does not extend its destruction deadline. The test manager will provide supplemental proof when the item is destroyed.

We accept the access attachment and the three-business-day substitution procedure. Please carry forward the requirement that every named recipient be bound in writing by confidentiality and use terms at least as protective as the agreement before receiving material. The testing house remains responsible for its recipients. The agreed tests are the sole permitted use, and the prohibition on using the material to develop or assist in developing a competing product applies to source files, extracts and derivative fixtures alike.

We accept the ten-business-day fallback with this clarification.

> Expiry of the review period triggers closeout only. Report acceptance requires written confirmation. If the design owner requests a correction within the review period, the original closeout deadline continues to apply to all material except the files and fixtures needed for that correction. The corrected-report review period applies only to those items. Earlier termination starts closeout for all remaining items and does not extend a deadline already running.

The testing house may retain the agreed geometry-free report. The two-year limit applies only to the specified geometry-free calibration records, which the testing house will delete at expiry. We agree that no backup exception is needed.

We accept the proposed wording on remote verification and closeout, including the distinction between the report review deadline and written acceptance. We also agree to delete each geometry-free calibration record two years after its calibration date.

The access attachment will require every named recipient to be bound in writing, before disclosure, by confidentiality and use terms at least as protective as the agreement. We remain responsible for each recipient, including an approved substitute. The sole-use and competing-product restrictions apply to source files, working copies, extracts, fixture files and physical fixtures. This resolves the outstanding terms.

We request a narrow addendum for the prototype batch. Only the geometry on page 4 of one drawing is export-restricted. We propose the following wording.

> The design owner will identify the affected drawing by number and revision in the access attachment and supply a test copy with the page 4 geometry removed, including from any embedded data. The design owner will withhold the original drawing and any extract or fixture file that reveals that geometry. If the testing house or a specialist has already received such material, it will stop using it, prevent further access and notify the design owner promptly so the parties can arrange secure disposition. Work that does not depend on the restricted geometry may proceed under the agreed terms.
>
> The design owner will prepare an alternative reference coupon that does not disclose the restricted geometry within two days after the parties agree in writing on a verification test. Before using the coupon for the batch, the testing house will run the agreed test and send the results to the design owner for written release. The existing access, use and closeout terms apply to the coupon and its accompanying files.

We propose a low-level vibration sweep with the coupon mounted in the intended test setup. We can provide a geometry-free reference response for comparison. Please confirm whether that check would verify the setup for your batch test and propose the measurement locations, frequency range and pass/fail tolerances you would use. Please also confirm whether any recipient already holds the affected drawing once we identify its number and revision.

We accept the redacted-copy and secure-disposition wording. The shop has already cut stock for the original fixture. We will hold that stock and pause further machining. Once you identify the drawing number and revision, we will check our holdings and obtain written confirmations from the shop and lab. We will report who received any affected material and whether the stock incorporates restricted geometry. We will use the stock only if you clear it in writing.

We propose the following additions for the prototype batch.

> **Custody and machining.** The design owner will deliver the coupon directly to the testing house. It will remain in the test lead’s custody at the testing house through verification and batch testing, then be returned directly to the design owner with receipt recorded for closeout. The test lead may measure the coupon on site. The design owner will specify the machining tolerances and approve the completed, geometry-free tolerance table in writing before the test lead sends it to the named shop personnel. The shop will receive only that table for the coupon work.
>
> **Setup check and release.** We propose measuring input acceleration at the fixture base near the mounting interface and response acceleration at a design-owner-designated point on the coupon, both along the sweep axis. We will run a low-level sweep over the frequency range covered by your reference response and the intended batch test, then remove and independently remount the coupon and repeat the sweep. Before the check, please confirm that the reference covers the required batch range and specify the frequency endpoints, input level, measurement points, allowable deviation from the reference and allowable difference between mountings. Both runs must meet the reference limits and the pair must meet the repeatability limit. We will submit both traces and the comparison. Batch testing will start only after your written release. A failed check requires corrective action and a repeat check before release.
>
> **Timing.** The two-day coupon preparation period starts when both parties approve the written check and its limits. We propose moving the scheduled batch start and report date by two days. Please confirm the coupon delivery time and a reviewer who can issue a release or identify a failed criterion within one business day of receiving the results. If delivery, a failed check or pending release affects the revised dates, we will agree new dates in writing. Work independent of the restricted geometry can continue during the hold.

With agreed limits and a reference covering the batch range, we would accept this check to verify the mounting and measurement setup for the batch.

We accept the stock hold, direct delivery, test-lead custody and return of the coupon against a recorded receipt. Once we identify the drawing number and revision in the access attachment, please include the cut stock and any associated machining files in the holdings check. Keep both on hold pending our written disposition. The test lead may measure the coupon on site for the agreed setup and machining tasks. Only the geometry-free tolerance table we approve in writing may go to the named shop personnel.

We accept the proposed two-sweep check. The test lead will measure input acceleration at the fixture base near the mounting interface and response acceleration at the designated coupon point, both along the sweep axis. The second run requires removal and independent remounting. Each run must meet the reference limits across the full batch range, and the two runs must meet the agreed repeatability limit. After a failed check, the testing house will document the correction and repeat both runs.

Please send the intended batch frequency endpoints and the lab’s proposed low-level input amplitude. Our project engineer will confirm reference coverage and provide the geometry-free reference, marked measurement points, comparison method and numerical acceptance limits for joint written approval. That approval starts the two-day preparation period.

We agree to move the scheduled batch start and report date by two days. At check approval, we will confirm dispatch and expected delivery separately and identify our authorized release reviewer by name. Within one business day of receiving both traces and the comparison, that reviewer will issue written release, identify the failed criterion, or specify any missing result needed for a decision. Batch testing requires written release. If delivery, a repeat check or pending release affects either revised date, we will agree the new date with you in writing.

We agree to the two-sweep signoff procedure and the two-day shift in both the batch start and report date. We will confirm the batch frequency endpoints against the test plan, obtain the lab’s proposed low-level input amplitude, and send all three values with their units and the amplitude convention. The two-day coupon preparation period begins when both parties approve the complete check in writing. Batch testing requires written release from your named reviewer.

Once you identify the drawing number and revision, we will report the holdings at the testing house, shop and lab, including the cut stock and associated machining files. Both remain on hold pending your written disposition. Please include your specified machining tolerances with the coupon instructions so our test lead can prepare the geometry-free table for your written approval before sending it to the named shop personnel.

We will include the specified machining tolerances with the coupon instructions. The test lead may use them to prepare the geometry-free table. Only the table we approve in writing may be sent to the named shop personnel.

This settles the addendum wording. We will provide the drawing number and revision in the access attachment to initiate the holdings check. Once we receive the confirmed frequency endpoints and proposed input amplitude with units and amplitude convention, our project engineer will return the complete check and numerical limits for joint written approval.
